text:
zara: Heads-up 15min: we need to lock the default connectivity mode for private deployments. Three viable modes: relay (our SNAT relay), customer-egress (customer supplies static egress IPs / NAT), and peering (BGP / dedicated link). Goal: pick default for GA + define safe upgrade/rollback path.

leo: My vote is relay-as-default. Fastest for customers, minimal NetOps touch. We should add explicit capacity limits and metrics so we can detect IP pool saturation early.

ana: Agree relay default. Important: some enterprise customers will require certified egress IP ownership and no shared relay. We need an opt-in flow for customer-egress and a clear SLO for failover.

devops-lee: Peering is heavy contracts + ASN + testing. Recommend tie peering to Dedicated plans only. For peering readiness checklist include: BGP timers, prefix filters, MTU, path MTU tests, and a pre-cutover traffic mirroring step.

field-sam: From field reports: customers expect a "no config" onboarding. Relay covers that. But add an operator toggle so CS can flip a tenant to customer-egress without doing a full redeploy.

zara: Proposal: GA default = relay; customer-egress = self-serve opt-in with validation checks; peering = Dedicated-only gated feature. Fallback semantics: agent runs liveness + conn-check to egress targets; on 3 consecutive failures revert to relay automatically and surface reason in Console.

leo: Need API design for toggle. Sketch: POST /api/v1/tenants/:tenant_id/connectivity -> { mode: "relay|egress|peering", egress_ips: ["203.0.113.5"], asn: "64521" } GET returns status + last_probe_time + probe_health. Also include a dry-run validation endpoint.

ana: Add IPv6 story: some customers are IPv6-only. Relay must support NAT64 or an IPv6 egress path. If customer-egress provides only IPv6, we should accept and document constraints.

devops-lee: Packaging checklist items: agent config flags for mode, firewall egress ports, DNS stub entries, TLS termination notes, healthcheck endpoints (tcp:443, http:/health), and instructions for IP rotation. Add a K8s operator CRD example for flipping mode.

field-sam: On migrations: support zero-downtime switch where TCP sockets are drained gracefully, and KV cache warming is attempted on target path. If metrics degrade beyond threshold during migration, auto-revert. Define thresholds in acceptance criteria.

zara: Acceptance criteria (GA): 1) Relay default deploy works end-to-end with onboarding template, 2) Customer-egress opt-in flow validates IP reachability + ownership, 3) Console shows per-tenant connectivity mode + last probe result, 4) Automatic fallback to relay after 3 failed probes with audit log entry, 5) Peering documented and gated behind Dedicated SLA.

leo: Ops items: simulate IP pool exhaustion in staging, run scale test with 10k tenants. Also document billing implications for relay egress.

ana: Security: require customers to register egress IPs in portal and sign an SLA that they will not route arbitrary traffic through our relay. Add rate-limiting per-tenant in relay.

devops-lee: I'll draft the migration CRD + example commands today and add a failover smoke test script: `scripts/connectivity_check.sh tenant-id`.

infra-bot: infra-bot: Created draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/private-connectivity-ga-plan (comment-enabled) :robot_face:

zara: Great. Next steps: Lee -> CRD + smoke test, Leo -> relay sizing doc and cost model, Ana -> IPv6 + compliance notes, Sam -> field checklist + CS playbook. I'll update the roadmap ticket and schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow.

(ended)
